title: Synthetic Biology
hook: If genetic engineering edits life's existing code, synthetic biology aims to engineer it from the ground up — designing new biological parts and even whole systems.
key_points: Synthetic biology designs and builds new biological parts, devices, and systems.
It treats genes like standardized parts that can be combined like engineering components.
Scientists can program cells to make medicines, fuels, materials, or to sense chemicals.
It raises questions about safety, biosecurity, and how far to redesign life.
content_html: Genetic engineering usually edits genes that already exist. Synthetic biology is more ambitious: it treats biology as an engineering discipline, aiming to design and build new biological parts, circuits, and even whole genetic systems. The mindset is to make life's components modular and predictable — genes that snap together like standardized parts.
extra_html: As Encyclopaedia Britannica describes, synthetic biologists assemble genetic "parts" into circuits that give cells new behaviors: bacteria that glow when they detect a toxin, yeast engineered to brew a precursor of the antimalarial drug artemisinin, or microbes coaxed into producing fuels and novel materials. The field pushes toward genomes designed largely on a computer and written into living cells. That power brings real concern — about accidental release, biosecurity, and how far it is wise to redesign living things — which is why safety and governance are central to the conversation around it.

related.title: GMOs and Genetic Engineering
related.hook: By deliberately rewriting an organism's DNA, scientists can make bacteria brew human insulin or crops resist pests — traits nature never handed them.

related.title: What Is Biotechnology?
related.hook: From cheese and beer to insulin and vaccines, biotechnology puts living things — or their molecular parts — to work making products we need.

related.title: CRISPR: Molecular Scissors for DNA
related.hook: Borrowed from a bacterial immune system, CRISPR lets scientists find a precise spot in the genome and cut it — turning gene editing into something almost routine.

flashcards.prompt: How does synthetic biology differ from ordinary genetic engineering?
flashcards.back_html: Rather than tweaking existing genes, synthetic biology aims to design and build new biological parts and systems, treating life's components like engineering blocks that can be combined to order.

flashcards.prompt: What is a core idea of synthetic biology?

choices.text: Treating genes as standardized parts that can be assembled into new systems
Avoiding all use of DNA in experiments
Only studying organisms without changing them

flashcards.explanation_html: Synthetic biology borrows from engineering: it tries to make genetic components modular and predictable, so cells can be programmed for new jobs.

flashcards.prompt: Which is a real application of synthetic biology?

choices.text: Engineering yeast to brew a malaria drug normally extracted from a plant
Building a bridge out of recycled steel

flashcards.explanation_html: Programming microbes to manufacture drugs, fuels, or materials is a hallmark of synthetic biology — for example, engineering yeast to produce a precursor of the antimalarial drug artemisinin.
